findings.title: Local cache is populated before the store call, so a device rejected by the limit is accepted on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI sets the device key in localCache (29-minute TTL) before calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key is already cached, so the next request from the same device hits the cache and returns nil, and Anonymous.Authenticate then issues an anonymous identity. The device limit is therefore bypassed by simply reloading the page once; it only becomes enforced again after the cache entry expires, producing an inconsistent allow/deny pattern. The cache entry should only be set after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice (or be removed on error).

findings.title: Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic; concurrent requests can exceed the limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads CountDevices in one session and then performs the insert in a separate session with no transaction or lock. Several new devices authenticating concurrently (and across multiple Grafana instances) will all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, so the number of active anonymous devices can exceed the configured device_limit by the number of concurrent requests. If the limit is meant to be a hard cap (e.g. for licensing), it needs a transactional check or a DB-level guard.

findings.title: rowsAffected==0 is treated as 'limit reached', which misfires on MySQL when the UPDATE changes nothing
findings.body: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever RowsAffected() is 0. With go-sql-driver/mysql (default, no clientFoundRows) RowsAffected reports rows actually changed, not rows matched. If an existing, in-window device re-tags with identical client_ip/user_agent and an updated_at that rounds to the same second (MySQL datetime precision), the UPDATE matches but changes nothing, RowsAffected is 0, and a legitimately known device is wrongly rejected with 'device limit reached'. Distinguish 'row not found' (e.g. via a preceding SELECT or FOUND_ROWS semantics) from 'row unchanged'.

findings.title: Mutating captured args inside WithDbSession callback breaks if the callback is retried
findings.body: updateDevice (copying the existing pattern in CreateOrUpdateDevice) does `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` inside the WithDbSession closure. sqlstore's WithDbSession retries the callback on SQLite 'database is locked' errors; on a retry the query string is prepended a second time, producing an Exec call with the query as both the statement and the first bind argument, which fails with a parameter-count error. Build the full argument slice outside the closure.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from a background goroutine into the synchronous auth path
findings.body: Previously TagDevice ran in a detached goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and panic recovery, so DB latency never affected anonymous request latency. It now runs inline in Authenticate using the request context: for every device not in the 29-minute local cache the request pays for a COUNT(*) over anon_device plus an upsert before any identity is returned, and a slow or unavailable DB (or request-context cancellation) now surfaces on the hot path for all anonymous traffic. The panic recovery is also gone. If synchronous enforcement is required only when a limit is configured, consider keeping the async path when AnonymousDeviceLimit == 0, and/or avoiding the count query when no limit is set (already partially done) and the upsert cost when possible.

findings.title: ErrDeviceLimitReached is a plain fmt.Errorf, giving users an opaque auth failure
findings.body: When the limit is reached Authenticate returns anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached, which is a bare fmt.Errorf value rather than an errutil error with a public message/status. The authn service will surface it as a generic authentication failure, so operators and end users get no indication that the anonymous device limit was hit. Consider defining it with errutil (e.g. a 401/403 with a public message) so the frontend can show a meaningful message.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit declared as `undefined` literal type, and backend never sends undefined
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` without an annotation makes TypeScript infer the property type as `undefined`, so `config.anonymousDeviceLimit > 0` or any numeric use will not compile for consumers. In addition, the Go DTO field is a non-pointer int64 without omitempty, so the backend always sends a number (0 when unset) and the value is never undefined at runtime. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` (or `number = 0` to match the backend).

findings.title: Limit tests do not cover the update-existing-device path or the service/auth behavior
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a second new device is rejected. It does not verify that an already-tagged device can still be updated once the limit is reached (the updateDevice path), that a device older than the 30-day window counts as new, or that Anonymous.Authenticate returns an error (and that the local cache does not mask it) when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. The impl_test cases all use setting.NewCfg() with a zero limit, so the new config plumbing through ProvideAnonymousDeviceService is untested.
